reply.title: The Vertical Throw
reply.story:
When you toss a ball straight up into the air, it slows down as it climbs, stops for the briefest instant at its highest point, and then speeds up as it falls back down. Watching it pause at the top, it is easy to wonder if everything stops completely--including the pull of gravity. If the velocity is zero at the peak, does the acceleration vanish too?

Galileo showed that heavy and light objects change their speed at a steady rate under gravity, regardless of whether they are moving up, resting at the top, or moving down. The velocity passes smoothly through zero, but the rate of change--the acceleration--remains constant throughout the flight.
reply.cardDescription: Explore a ball thrown straight up. See how velocity changes while acceleration stays constant at $-g$, even at the peak where velocity is $0$.
reply.instructions: Adjust the launch speed and press Play to watch the motion. Use the scrubber to explore different moments in time.
